attribution.note: These are Zitron's own words in his own post, followed by his own figures.

semantics.note: A present-tense observation about his own 'diversified revenue' measure over fiscal Q1–Q3 2026. The paraphrase about revenue outside the largest buyers matches his definition.

contract.note: The contract uses his own measure and the quarters he named. Treating a fall of about a quarter or more as 'collapsing' is an ordinary reading. Caveats: the measure moves mechanically when customers cross the 10% line, and it reflects direct buyers rather than end demand.

evidence.note: Reported 10-Q shares match his Q1 (16%/14%) and Q2 (23%/16%) figures. The same article also reports four more 10%-plus customers in Q2, which would undercut his Q2 figure.
Q1 revenue of $44.1B minus the top two customers' 30% leaves about $30.9B, in line with his $30.84B.
The quoted Q3 10-Q shows four customers at 61% of $57B, leaving about $22.2B. That is roughly 28% below Q1.
Reports four more 10%-plus customers in Q2. If correct, Q2 would sit far below Q3, so the path was not steady, but the Q1-to-Q3 fall still holds.
Direct customers are likely distributors and server makers, so his measure tracks direct-customer concentration, not end-demand diversity.

reviews.rationale: On his own measure, revenue outside 10%-plus direct customers fell from about $30.9B in Q1 to about $22.2B in Q3, roughly 28%. That meets the contract's bar. The disputed Q2 figures would make the path uneven and his Q2 number wrong, but they do not remove the Q1-to-Q3 decline. The measure's mechanical and end-demand limits are noted but do not change the result on his stated metric.

attribution.note: Zitron's own assertion in his own post.

semantics.note: In context he means there is little AI compute demand outside OpenAI and Anthropic. The qualifier is kept.

contract.note: The plain reading (demand outside the two labs is a minor residual compared with their demand, Jan–Sep 2025) is ordinary and not stretched. It sensibly declines to invent a numeric threshold.

evidence.note: CoreWeave's 10-Q shows Microsoft at 67% of its revenue but does not say how much of that served OpenAI, and it does not measure the wider market.
Google's own disclosure shows rapid growth in generative-AI product revenue and outside customers, but no measure of raw compute spending. It is a company disclosure.
Backlog and Meta's commitment are future commitments, not realized revenue in the target period.

reviews.rationale: None of the evidence measures realized AI compute spending outside OpenAI and Anthropic for Jan–Sep 2025 with indirect purchases removed. CoreWeave's concentration, Google's product growth and Meta's commitment hint at both sides but cannot settle whether the remaining market was a minor residual.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own post.

semantics.note: A firm conditional ('will') with its antecedent kept, bundled with a universal premise about present funding dependence. The paraphrase is faithful.

contract.note: Counting any AI startup closure, such as Yupp, as 'one of these companies' stretches his words against him. Small startups fold routinely. In context, 'current stack' points to the major, heavily funded AI companies. Under that reading the antecedent is unknown from the packet.

evidence.note: Yupp's closure is real and dated after the post. Whether it meets the antecedent depends on a disputed reading, so it bears on the condition, not on the outcome.

Record AI share of venture deal value through Q3 2026 weighs against a 'narrative death'. But the totals include money raised before the closure, and fundraising and exits are described as constrained.

reviews.rationale: No deadline was given and no conclusive event is shown. On a fair reading, the antecedent (one of the main AI companies failing) is not established, so the conditional is not scored. Even on the contract's broad Yupp reading, the evidence does not isolate a post-closure effect on fundraising or acquisitions. The universal funding-dependence premise is also untested.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own post.

semantics.note: A firm 'will' forecast with only 'eventually' as the horizon. The context is bank lending to AI data centers, and the paraphrase is close enough.

contract.note: It is reasonable to focus on unpaid loan payments for AI data center projects and treat 'eventually' as an open horizon. Its early-support rule is fair.

evidence.note: A tracker reports no public neocloud default on a GPU-backed loan as of October 2026. That is absence before a deadline, not failure.
Oracle's force-majeure notice on Project Jupiter signals stress but is not a missed loan payment. Oracle says the project is on schedule.

reviews.rationale: No documented missed payment or default on an AI data center loan appears by the evaluation date, so the early-support rule is not met. With no deadline, the absence of defaults does not contradict the forecast. It remains open.
